blind_analysis.reference: The coding is important. You write instructions for the Arduino. You can make the arm pick up small things. You can move them to a new spot.
blind_analysis.reproduction: The coding is important. The Arduino writes instructions for you. You can make the arm pick up small things. You can move them to a new spot.

differences.learner_form: The Arduino writes instructions for you.
differences.corrected_form: You write instructions for the Arduino.
differences.description: Subject and object of 'write instructions' are swapped (agent/recipient reversal): reference has the learner writing instructions for the Arduino; reproduction has the Arduino writing instructions for the learner. This inverts who performs the action.

rationale: Only one difference exists between reference and reproduction (sentence 2). It is not a surface morphology/agreement/particle issue but a full agent-swap that inverts the meaning of the sentence (who instructs whom), matching the README's critical criterion ('meaning lost/inverted/misleading'). Of the v5 EN subtypes available (no dedicated meaning-inversion subtype exists in v5), 'word_choice' (fidelity dimension) is the closest fit for a whole-meaning substitution, over 'word_order' (pure syntactic reordering) or 'pronoun_reference' (anaphora resolution, not applicable here since 'you'/'the Arduino' are not co-referential pronouns).
